// One function engineered to clear the very_high (>25) threshold, so the
// golden proves BuildFileResult's strict ">" comparison against a real
// measured number rather than an assumed one.
int monster(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e) {
    if (a > 0 && b > 0) { return 1; }
    if (a > 1 && b > 1) { return 1; }
    if (a > 2 && b > 2) { return 1; }
    if (a > 3 && b > 3) { return 1; }
    if (a > 4 && b > 4) { return 1; }
    if (a > 5 && b > 5) { return 1; }
    if (a > 6 && b > 6) { return 1; }
    if (a > 7 && b > 7) { return 1; }
    if (a > 8 && b > 8) { return 1; }
    if (a > 9 && b > 9) { return 1; }
    switch (c) {
        case 0: break;
        case 1: break;
        case 2: break;
        case 3: break;
        case 4: break;
    }
    return d > e ? d : e;
}

// A small function in the same file, to prove the very-high row does not
// contaminate a neighbour's count.
int quiet(int a) {
    return a + 1;
}
